lead: Each story names who, what, and why. Open one for confirmation and the walk.

items.name: Portfolio
items.statusNote: The live prototype already walks this.
items.summary: See use across the estate, a group, or a site.
items.who: A Customer uses Portfolio. Viewer can look. Contributor can work.

sections.name: Tree
sections.summary: Find and pick a place on the estate

sections.name: Consumption
sections.summary: Read use on the graph for a group or a site

sections.name: Site profile
sections.summary: See and set hours, time of use, and attributes for each site and meter

stories.name: Scan the estate
stories.want: see All and the named groups in the Portfolio tree
stories.benefit: I can start from the whole estate before I pick a group or site
stories.notes: This is the first look at Portfolio. The pane opens on the Consumption tab. Other tabs have their own stories.

criteria.given: I am on the Portfolio page
criteria.when: the tree on the left loads
criteria.then: All sits at the top of the tree with its site count in grey, such as 107 sites

criteria.given: All is selected in the Portfolio tree
criteria.when: I look at the pane on the right
criteria.then: the kicker reads the company, the heading reads All, and the line below gives the number of sites and meter points

criteria.given: I am on the Portfolio page
criteria.when: I click a group in the tree
criteria.then: the group opens with its sites under it, each with a grey meter count, and the other groups hide

criteria.given: a group is open in the Portfolio tree
criteria.when: I click the group again
criteria.then: its sites hide

stages.name: All on the tree
stages.caption: All sits at the top. The pane is the collective overview.

stages.name: A group open
stages.caption: The group shows its sites. Opening one group closes the others.

dev.why: More than Search. Tree, All, and group accordion.

test.why: Check All, each group, and a long tree that scrolls

stories.name: Find a site or meter
stories.want: search the Portfolio tree for a site or meter
stories.benefit: I can reach it without opening every group
stories.notes: The Filter icon button sits to the right of Search. Filter has its own story, Filter the tree.

criteria.given: I am on the Portfolio page
criteria.when: I look at the top of the tree
criteria.then: a Search field reads Search site or meter, with the Filter icon button to its right

criteria.given: I am on the Portfolio page
criteria.when: I type a site name or meter number in Search
criteria.then: the tree shows only the matching sites and meters

criteria.given: Search in the Portfolio tree has text in it
criteria.when: I leave the Portfolio page and come back
criteria.then: Search is empty and the tree shows every group

stages.name: Search the tree
stages.caption: Type a site or meter. Hits sit in the tree.

dev.why: This is the 2. Search, then hits in the tree.

test.why: This is the 2. Type a name, then check the hits in the tree

stories.name: Filter the tree
stories.want: filter the Portfolio tree by utility type and by incoming or outgoing
stories.benefit: the tree only shows sites and meters that match
stories.notes: The same filters sit behind the Filter icon button at the top right of the pane. The prototype has no ownership filter, so confirm whether it is needed. Confirm the component name for the removable filter Tag against the component library.

criteria.given: I am on the Portfolio page
criteria.when: I pick the Filter icon button to the right of Search
criteria.then: an overlay opens with a Utility type Select (All, Electricity, Gas, and Water) and an Incoming and outgoing Select (All, In, and Out), each option with its site count

criteria.given: the Filter overlay is open in the Portfolio tree
criteria.when: I pick Gas in Utility type
criteria.then: the tree only shows sites with a gas meter

criteria.given: a filter is on in the Portfolio tree
criteria.when: I look under Search
criteria.then: each filter shows as a removable Tag with a Clear text button after them, and the Filter icon button shows a teal count

criteria.given: filter Tags show under Search
criteria.when: I pick the cross on a Tag, or pick Clear
criteria.then: that filter goes, or every filter goes

criteria.given: the Filter overlay is open in the Portfolio tree
criteria.when: I pick Clear all at the bottom of the overlay
criteria.then: every filter goes and the tree shows every site

stages.name: Filter overlay
stages.caption: Ticks for Ownership, Meter, and Incoming and Outgoing.

stages.name: Filter pills
stages.caption: Pills sit under Search. A cross clears that one.

dev.why: Overlay ticks, pills, count, and Clear.

test.why: Each filter alone and together, the count, and Clear

stories.name: Read a group
stories.want: see consumption for a group
stories.benefit: I can read the total for the group without opening each site
stories.notes: Cost, Carbon, Site profile, Alerts, and Queries have their own stories. Each pill under the group heading is a site.

criteria.given: I am on the Portfolio page
criteria.when: I click a group in the tree
criteria.then: the pane kicker reads the company, such as EDF, and the heading reads the group name

criteria.given: I am on a group in Portfolio
criteria.when: the Consumption tab is selected
criteria.then: the graph shows the total for the sites that are on

criteria.given: I am on a group in Portfolio
criteria.when: I look under the heading
criteria.then: each site shows as a pill, with a Show more text button when there are many

criteria.given: site pills show under the group heading
criteria.when: I click a site pill
criteria.then: that site leaves the graph and its name strikes through, and this works for the last site too

stages.name: Group pane
stages.caption: Collective consumption. Each pill is a site.

dev.why: Collective graph and site pills.

test.why: Needs a group with sites of each utility. The group total must equal the sum of its sites

stories.name: Read a site
stories.want: see incoming and outgoing on one graph for a site
stories.benefit: I can read import and export together
stories.notes: Do not put All, In, or Out chips in the site header. Do not put a meter Select in the site header.

criteria.given: I am on a site in Portfolio that has In and Out channels
criteria.when: the Consumption tab loads
criteria.then: the graph title reads Incoming and outgoing

criteria.given: I am on a site in Portfolio that has In and Out channels
criteria.when: I look at the key under the graph
criteria.then: In is teal with an import mark and Out is black with an export mark

criteria.given: the key under the graph shows In and Out
criteria.when: I click one
criteria.then: that series leaves the graph and its name strikes through, and this works for the last one too

criteria.given: I am on a site in Portfolio
criteria.when: I look under the heading
criteria.then: each meter shows as a pill with its number, even when there is only one

stages.name: Site pane
stages.caption: Incoming and outgoing. In is cyan. Out is black.

dev.why: Incoming and Outgoing, the key, and meter pills.

test.why: Needs a site that both imports and exports

stories.name: Change the window
stories.want: change the date window of the graph
stories.benefit: I can read a preset window or a custom from and to
stories.notes: Gaps stay gaps. Zero is a reading.

criteria.given: I am on a graph tab in Portfolio, such as Consumption
criteria.when: I open the date Select at the top right of the pane
criteria.then: I can pick Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, Last month, Last 12 months, or Custom

criteria.given: the date Select is open
criteria.when: I pick Custom
criteria.then: a calendar opens where I set from and to, and the dates next to the graph title change to match

criteria.given: a preset is on in the date Select
criteria.when: I use the previous and next arrows at the top right of the graph
criteria.then: the window moves and the date Select reads Custom, then reads the preset again when I return to the first window

criteria.given: the graph shows the latest window
criteria.when: I look at the next arrow
criteria.then: it is off

stages.name: Date on the graph
stages.caption: The preset name sits next to the title. Arrows sit to the right.

dev.why: Date Select, Custom calendar, and arrows.

test.why: The edges of each window, Custom ranges, and the arrows at each end

stories.name: Switch the graph
stories.want: change the view and the chart type of the graph
stories.benefit: I can add readings up or break them down, and pick bars or lines
stories.notes: Cost and Carbon have their own stories. In and Out stay teal and black bars when Total consumption and Bar are on. Overlay, Average profile, Highlight weekends, and Restore defaults also sit in Chart settings and wait for their own stories.

criteria.given: I am on the Consumption tab in Portfolio
criteria.when: I pick Chart settings, the secondary pill button with a gear icon next to the graph title
criteria.then: I see a View Select with Total consumption, Individual consumption, and Calendar, and a Chart type control with Bar and Line

criteria.given: Total consumption and Bar are on in Chart settings
criteria.when: I read the graph
criteria.then: it adds the readings up as bars

criteria.given: I am on a group in Portfolio
criteria.when: I pick Individual consumption and Line in Chart settings
criteria.then: I see one line for each site

criteria.given: I am on a site in Portfolio
criteria.when: I pick Individual consumption and Line in Chart settings
criteria.then: I see one line for each meter

criteria.given: I am on a group in Portfolio
criteria.when: I pick Total consumption and Line in Chart settings
criteria.then: I see one line for the total

stages.name: Individual consumption
stages.caption: Lines, one per site on a group, or one per meter on a site.

dev.why: Bars or lines, and group vs site.

test.why: Bars and lines at group and site level

stories.name: See Cost
stories.want: see the Cost tab for the same window
stories.benefit: I can read spend in pounds
stories.notes: The rates in Attributes in Site settings feed the numbers. Water uses £ too.

criteria.given: I am on a group or a site in Portfolio
criteria.when: I pick the Cost tab
criteria.then: the graph title reads Cost and the axis reads £

criteria.given: I am on the Cost tab in Portfolio
criteria.when: I open the View Select in Chart settings
criteria.then: I can pick Total cost or Individual cost

stages.name: Cost on the pane
stages.caption: Same window as Consumption. The unit is £.

dev.why: Same graph as Consumption. The unit is £.

test.why: Check the ? figure against the tariff for a known day

stories.name: See Carbon
stories.want: see the Carbon tab for the same window
stories.benefit: I can read kgCO2e for the same places
stories.notes: Water uses the 2026 supply and wastewater factors, added together on the graph.

criteria.given: I am on a group or a site in Portfolio
criteria.when: I pick the Carbon tab
criteria.then: the graph title reads Carbon and the axis reads kgCO2e

criteria.given: I am on the Carbon tab in Portfolio
criteria.when: I open the View Select in Chart settings
criteria.then: I can pick Total carbon or Individual carbon

stages.name: Carbon on the pane
stages.caption: Same window as Consumption. The unit is kgCO2e.

dev.why: Same graph as Consumption. The unit is kgCO2e.

test.why: Check the kgCO2e figure against the factor for a known day

stories.name: Compare others
stories.want: compare other places at the same level
stories.benefit: I can add more than one place to the graph
stories.notes: On a meter, Compare lists other meters across the portfolio. Each row shows the site and the MPAN.

criteria.given: I am on All or a group in Portfolio
criteria.when: I look at the top right of the pane
criteria.then: the Compare button reads Compare groups

criteria.given: I am on a site in Portfolio
criteria.when: I look at the top right of the pane
criteria.then: the Compare button reads Compare sites

criteria.given: I am on a site in Portfolio
criteria.when: I pick Compare sites
criteria.then: a Modal opens with the line Search and add other sites at this level, a Search field, a Filter, and a row for each site with an Add button

criteria.given: the Compare Modal is open
criteria.when: I pick Add on two rows and then Done
criteria.then: both sites join the graph

criteria.given: I have added places to compare
criteria.when: I look at the Compare button
criteria.then: it shows a teal count, and its cross clears the comparison

stages.name: Compare modal
stages.caption: Search, Filter, and a list of others at that level.

dev.why: Modal, more than one place, and lines on the graph.

test.why: More than one place, the lines, and the Modal at each level

stories.name: Compare site profiles
stories.want: see the operational hours, time of use, floor area, and occupants of every site in one table
stories.benefit: I can spot gaps across a group without opening each site
stories.notes: Shows on All and on a group. Download template and Upload are secondary pill buttons at the top right of the Site profile tab, above the table, with Upload on the right. Upload has its own story. A Custom Tag means the hours or time of use were set by hand with no saved preset.

criteria.given: I am on All or a group in Portfolio
criteria.when: I pick the Site profile tab
criteria.then: a table lists each site with the columns Site, Operational hours, Time of use, Floor area, and Occupants

walk.note: A table lists each site with the columns Site, Operational hours, Time of use, Floor area, and Occupants.

criteria.given: every meter on a site uses the same week preset
criteria.when: I look at the Operational hours or Time of use column in its row
criteria.then: the Tag shows the preset name, or Custom if no preset is saved

The Tag shows the preset name, or Custom if no preset is saved.

criteria.when: I look at the Operational hours or Time of use column in its row

criteria.when: I hover a Tag in the Operational hours or Time of use column

walk.note: A Tooltip opens with each day of the week and its times.

criteria.when: I pick Download template, the secondary pill button at the top right of the tab, to the left of Upload

walk.note: A file downloads that lists the sites in the table, ready to fill in.

criteria.given: I am on the Site profile tab at All or a group
criteria.when: I click a site row in the table
criteria.then: the Site profile tab opens for that site

walk.note: The Site profile tab opens for that site.

criteria.when: I pick a column header in the table

stages.caption: One row per site. Download template and Upload sit above the table.

stages.caption: Hover a tag to see each day of the week.

dev.why: A table of sites, Tags that fold many meters into one, week Tooltips, and the template

stories.name: Read a site profile
stories.want: see where a site is and how its hours and time of use are set
stories.benefit: I can check a site at a glance before I change anything
stories.notes: A Custom Tag means the hours or time of use were set by hand with no saved preset. A preset on a meter shows its name and the icon for that meter's utility. Floor area and occupants sit under Attributes on the site card.

walk.note: A site card shows a map with a pin on the left and the address beside it.

criteria.given: the hours or time of use on a site were set by hand with no saved preset
criteria.when: I look at the Operational hours or Time of use Tag on the site card
criteria.then: it reads Custom

criteria.given: a meter uses a saved preset
criteria.when: I look at the Time of use Tags on the site card
criteria.then: the Tag shows the preset name with the icon for that meter's utility

walk.note: Hover a Tag with a preset name
The Tag shows the preset name with the icon for that meter's utility.

criteria.given: I am on the Site profile tab for a site
criteria.when: I hover a Time of use Tag such as Weekday peak

criteria.when: I hover the Operational hours Tag
criteria.then: a Tooltip opens with each day of the week and its operational hours

walk.note: A Tooltip opens with each day of the week and its operational hours.

criteria.given: I am on the Site profile tab for a site
criteria.when: I pick Site settings, the secondary pill button at the top right of the site card

walk.note: Site settings opens for that site.

criteria.when: I hover a Tag on the site card

criteria.given: I am on the Site profile tab for a site
criteria.when: I look at Attributes on the site card
criteria.then: I see the floor area and the occupants, such as 1,200 m² · 18 people

stages.name: Site profile
stages.caption: The map, address, hours, time of use, and attributes. Site settings sits to the right.

stages.name: Week on hover
stages.caption: Hover a preset to see on peak and off peak for each day.

dev.why: Map, address, and Tags. The Tooltip reuses the week Tooltip from the sites table

test.why: Needs a site with a map pin, an address, and a Tag in each column

stories.name: Read the meters on a site
stories.want: see each meter on a site with its channel, settings, last reading, and use
stories.benefit: I can tell which meters follow the site and which do not
stories.notes: From site means the meter takes the site settings, so three meters are set once, not three times. Change one meter and it becomes Custom. Use can also show a Partial Tag, so confirm what it means. Do not invent a SPID.

It gives the number of meters and lists each one with the columns Meter, Channel, Settings, Last reading, and Use.

stories.want: open the settings for a site
stories.benefit: I can change its hours, time of use, and attributes in one place
stories.notes: Each accordion has its own story. Upload has its own story. Viewers do not see the Site settings button. The prototype shows no message after Save changes and no prompt when you leave with changes. Both are gaps to close before build. Confirm where Save changes sits.

When other sites use the preset, the banner also names them, such as the times at Euston, Rugby, and 2 more sites.

estimate.help: Points are relative size, not days. Each story has two estimates. Find a site or meter is the 2 for both.

dev.help: Dev points size the work to build it. Complexity is how hard the logic is. Effort is how much there is to build. Risk is how likely it is to go wrong. Dependencies are what it needs from other teams or stories.

test.help: Test points size the work to check it. Scenarios are how many cases to run. Setup is the data and roles each case needs. Risk is how bad a missed bug would be. Regression is how much else needs a check again.
